question: A 48-year-old man who emigrated from Sri Lanka 2 years ago comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of fever, cough, and a 6-kg (13-lb) weight loss. He appears ill. An x-ray of the chest shows patchy infiltrates in the upper lung fields with a cavernous lesion at the right apex. A CT-guided biopsy of the lesion is obtained. A photomicrograph of the biopsy specimen is shown. Which of the following surface antigens is most likely to be found on the cells indicated by the arrow?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fever, cough, weight loss" -> "Suspicion of pulmonary tuberculosis" -> "Chest x-ray shows patchy infiltrates and cavernous lesion" -> "CT-guided biopsy obtained" -> "Photomicrograph of biopsy specimen shown" -> "Identification of surface antigen on cells indicated by the arrow" -> "CD56" -> 85%

analysis: The clinical presentation of a 48-year-old man with fever, cough, weight loss, and chest x-ray findings suggestive of a cavernous lesion at the right apex is highly suspicious for tuberculosis, especially in an immigrant from an endemic area like Sri Lanka. The photomicrograph of the biopsy specimen is likely to show cells expressing CD8 surface antigen, which is commonly found on cytotoxic T cells involved in the immune response against intracellular pathogens like Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
